newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's banking activity up in January.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's banking activity up in January.

text.p: The consolidated balance sheet of Lebanon's commercial banks rose, in dollar terms, to $24,085 million in January from $23,993 million in December 1996, the Lebanese Banks Association said on Monday.

Total deposits in foreign currencies and Lebanese pounds rose to 31,168 billion Lebanese pounds ($20,112 million) from 30,970 billion pounds ($19,955 million) at the end of December 1996, the association said in its latest monthly bulletin.
Lebanese pound deposits rose to 14,047 billion Lebanese pounds from 13,636 billion pounds.
Deposits in foreign currencies fell by $121 million to $11,048 million.
Dollarisation of banks deposits registered 54.93 percent against December's 55.97 percent.
Loans and credits to the private sector rose by 108 billion pounds in January to 13,398 billion Lebanese pounds from 13,290 billion pounds.

Credits in Lebanese pounds fell to 1,614 billion pounds in January from 1,623 billion pounds a month earlier while credits in foreign currencies to the private sector rose to $7,604 million from $7,517 million.
Loans and credits to the public sector rose by 48 billion pounds in January to 12,144 billion pounds.
